insights.insight: The protocol has produced 11,270 cryptographically verified purchase confirmations — not inferences, not modeled audiences. At a time when cookieless targeting forces brands back toward probabilistic proxies, this is the category of signal the ad industry claims to want but cannot currently buy at scale.

Cumulative verified GMV stands at $936,140 with velocity at 1.03x and acceleration at 1.003x — both above 1.0 simultaneously, meaning the pace is still building. The $1M crossing is 2-3 days out and is arriving through sustained compounding, not a promotional spike.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion pattern signals organic adoption
insights.insight: The network is expanding in pulse-then-quiet cycles — 14 new CBSAs in one heartbeat (rural OH, CA, ID, NE, IA non-metro), followed by only 2 the next — a rhythm consistent with social graph propagation rather than paid acquisition. Manufactured growth doesn't produce this breathing pattern.

insights.topic: Category breadth now spans physical retail through SaaS
insights.insight: Category entropy at 3.236 bits indicates no single vertical dominates; the receipt set covers grocery, fuel, dining, hardware, warehouse (Costco entered April 11), and as of April 9, digital SaaS subscriptions — the first non-physical-commerce category in network history. Basket CV of 0.55 confirms new categories are still entering.

insights.topic: Data flywheel runs whether brands engage or not
insights.insight: Each receipt submission adds a verified signal, rewards the submitter ~10 cents in bitcoin, and increases the analytical value of all prior signals through added context. The competitive implication for brands: the dataset accumulates on their category regardless of their participation.

insights.topic: Identity-free verified signals solve the privacy-utility tradeoff
insights.insight: Spend tokens carry no wallet reference in the signed payload — aggregate purchase behavior is verifiable without individual user identification. This is the architecture cookieless targeting has been promising: deterministic at the signal level, private at the identity level.
